jobs.name: Wiki Backlink Sweep (One-Time)
jobs.prompt:
ONE-TIME TASK: Add [[backlinks]] to wiki research files that have none.

This runs in a fresh session — be self-contained and thorough.

## Step 1: Find files needing backlinks

Run this search to find .md files in both wiki folders with zero `[[` links:
```bash
for f in $(find ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/research ~/.autognosia/oracle/brain -name "*.md" -not -path "*/graphify-out/*" -not -path "*/.git/*" 2>/dev/null); do
  if ! grep -q '[[' "$f"; then
    echo "$f"
  fi
done
```

Also check non-research files in active-wiki:
```bash
for f in $(find ~/.autognosia/active-wiki -name "*.md" -not -path "*/research/*" -not -path "*/graphify-out/*" -not -path "*/.git/*" -not -path "*/inbox/*" 2>/dev/null); do
  if ! grep -q '[[' "$f"; then
    echo "$f"
  fi
done
```

## Step 2: For each file without backlinks

1. Read the file to understand its topic
2. Look at the `tags:` and `sources:` frontmatter
3. Find related files by searching for overlapping tags/sources:
   ```bash
   grep -rl "tag1\|tag2" ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/research/ --include="*.md" 2>/dev/null | head -10
   ```
4. Add `[[wikilinks]]` inline in the content where concepts first appear. Format: `[[filename-without-extension]]`
5. Also add backlinks section at the end if appropriate:
   ```markdown
   ## Related
   - [[related-file-1]]
   - [[related-file-2]]
   ```

## Rules

- Every file should have at least 3-5 backlinks minimum
- Link on first mention of key concepts
- Don't link common words — only proper nouns, paper titles, system names, frameworks
- Prefer linking to other research files in the same folder
- Be conservative — better to under-link than over-link
- Verify each edit by re-reading the file

## Report

When done, output:
- Files modified: N
- Total backlinks added: N
- Files skipped (already had links): N
- Any errors encountered
